translations.title: Rhyme LVII: This Frame of Bones and Skin
Rhyme LXI: Watching My Feverish Hours
translations.text:
Watching my feverish hours
and sleepless hours pass slowly by,
at the side of my bed,
who will sit?

When I stretch out my trembling hand,
near to breathing my last,
seeking a friendly hand,
who will clasp it?

When death glazes over
the glass of my eyes,
my eyelids still open,
who will close them?

When the bell sounds
(if it sounds at my funeral),
on hearing it, who
will murmur a prayer?

When the earth at last weighs down
my pale remains,
at the forgotten grave,
who will come to weep?

Who, finally, on the next day,
when the sun shines again,
that I passed through this world—
who will remember?

translations.title: Rhyme XXVIII: When in the Dark Shadow
translations.text:
When, lost in the dark shadow,
a voice murmurs,
disturbing its mournful calm,
and deep within my soul
I hear its sweet echo,
tell me: is it the wind
moaning as it circles, or your sighs
speaking to me of love as they pass?

When the morning sun shines red
upon my window
and my love calls up your shadow,
if on my lips I seem to feel
the touch of other lips,
tell me: am I blindly dreaming,
or does your heart send me
a kiss upon a sigh?

If in the bright day
and in the deep, shadowed night,
in everything surrounding
the soul that longs for you,
I think I feel and see you,
tell me: do I touch and breathe
in a dream, or do you give me
your breath to drink upon a sigh?

translations.title: Rhyme LXXV: Can It Be True That Sleep
translations.text:
Can it be true that when sleep
touches our eyes with rosy fingers,
the spirit escapes the prison it inhabits
and takes hurried flight?

Can it be true that, a guest among the mists,
on the faint breath of the night breeze,
it rises winged into the empty realm
to meet with others?

And there, stripped of human form,
there, its earthly bonds broken,
does it dwell for a few brief hours
in the silent world of thought?

And does it laugh and weep, hate and love,
and leave a trace of sorrow and of joy,
like that a meteor leaves
as it crosses the sky?

I do not know whether that world of visions
lives outside us or within;
but I know that I know many people
whom I have never met!

translations.title: Rhyme LVI: Today Like Yesterday, Tomorrow Like Today
translations.text:
Today like yesterday, tomorrow like today,
and always the same!
A gray sky, an endless horizon,
and walking... walking!

Keeping time, like a stupid
machine, the heart;
the sluggish mind asleep
in a corner of the brain.

The soul, longing for a paradise,
seeking it without faith;
weariness without purpose, a wave rolling on
without knowing why.

A voice that endlessly, in the same tone,
sings the same song;
a monotonous drop of water falling,
and falling without end.

So the days go slipping by,
one after another,
today the same as yesterday... and all of them
without joy or pain.

Ah! sometimes I remember with a sigh
the suffering of old...
Pain is bitter; but at least
to suffer is to live!

translations.title: Rhyme XXXIV: She Passes Silently
translations.text:
She passes silently, and her movements
are a silent harmony;
her footsteps sound, and their sound recalls
the rhythmic cadence of a winged hymn.

She half opens her eyes, those eyes
as clear as day;
and earth and sky, all they encompass,
burn with new light in her pupils.

She laughs, and her laughter holds the notes
of running water;
she weeps, and every tear is a poem
of infinite tenderness.

She has the light, the fragrance,
the color and the line,
the form that gives birth to desire;
the expression, eternal source of poetry.

Is she stupid?... Bah! So long as she keeps
the riddle dark by keeping silent,
what she leaves unsaid will always be worth more,
to me, than anything another woman tells me.

translations.title: Rhyme XXXVII: Before You, I Shall Die in Hiding
translations.text:
Before you, I shall die in hiding;
already in my flesh
I carry the blade with which your hand
opened the wide mortal wound.

Before you I shall die, and my spirit,
stubborn in its purpose,
will sit down at the gates of death
and wait for you there.

Hours will fly with days, and days
with years,
and at last you will knock at that door...
Who does not knock at it?

Then, when the earth has taken
both your guilt and your remains,
washing you in the waters of death
as in another Jordan;

there, where the murmur of life
trembles and dies away
like a wave that comes to the shore
to expire in silence;

there, where the closing tomb
opens upon eternity...
all that we have both left unsaid
we shall have to speak!

translations.title: Rhyme LXXII: The Waves Have a Faint Harmony
translations.text:
FIRST VOICE

The waves have a faint harmony;
the violets, a gentle scent;
the cold night, mists of silver;
the day, light and gold;
I have something better:
I have Love.

SECOND VOICE

A breeze of applause, a radiant cloud,
a wave of envy kissing one's feet,
an island of dreams where the yearning
soul may rest,
a sweet intoxication:
that is Glory.

THIRD VOICE

Treasure is a burning coal,
vanity a fleeing shadow;
all is false: glory, gold.
What I adore
alone is true:
Liberty.

So the boatmen passed, singing
the eternal song,
and foam leapt at each stroke of the oar
and the sun struck it.

“Will you come aboard?” they cried. And I, smiling,
said to them as they passed:
“I did so long ago; indeed I still have
my clothes spread out to dry on the shore.”

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXVIII: Resting My Fevered Forehead
translations.text:
Resting my fevered forehead
against the cold windowpane,
in the silence of the dark night
I could not take my eyes from her balcony.

Amid the mysterious shadows
her window shone with light,
letting my gaze enter
the pure sanctuary of her room.

Her face pale as marble;
her fair hair unbraided,
its silken waves caressing
her alabaster shoulders and her throat—
my eyes beheld her, and my eyes,
seeing her so beautiful, grew troubled.

She looked at herself in the mirror; gently
she smiled at her lovely, languid image,
and its silent flattery in the glass
she repaid with a most tender kiss...

But the light went out; the pure vision
vanished like an empty shadow,
and I fell asleep, jealous of the glass
her lips had caressed.

translations.title: Rhyme LIII: The Dark Swallows Will Return
translations.text:
The dark swallows will return
to hang their nests upon your balcony,
and once again, playing, tap their wings
against your windowpanes.

But those whose flight was stayed
to watch your beauty and my happiness,
those that learned our names—
those will not return!

The thick honeysuckle will return
to climb your garden walls,
and once again, toward evening, its flowers
will open, more beautiful still.

But those laden with dew
whose drops we watched tremble
and fall like tears of the day—
those will not return!

Love's burning words will return
to sound in your ears;
perhaps your heart will wake
from its deep sleep.

But silent, rapt, and on my knees,
as God is worshipped before his altar,
as I have loved you... make no mistake,
no one will love you so!

translations.title: Rhyme LXXI: I Was Not Asleep
translations.text:
I was not asleep; I wandered in that limbo
where things change shape,
those mysterious spaces separating
waking from sleep.

The thoughts that silently circled
round and round my brain
began little by little to move
in a slower dance.

My eyelids veiled the reflection
of the light that enters the soul through the eyes;
but another light illuminated
the world of visions from within.

At that moment a murmur sounded in my ear,
like the indistinct sound that drifts
through a church when the faithful end
their prayers with an amen.

And I heard a thin, sad voice
calling my name from far away,
and smelled extinguished candles,
dampness and incense.

Night came, and into the arms of oblivion
I fell like a stone into its deep embrace;
I slept, and on waking cried: “Someone
I loved has died.”

translations.title: Rhyme XXV: When at Night You Are Wrapped
translations.text:
When at night you are wrapped
in the tulle wings of sleep
and your outspread eyelashes
resemble ebony arches,
to hear the beating
of your restless heart
and lay your sleeping head
upon my breast,
I would give, my soul,
all that I possess:
light, air,
and thought!

When your eyes are fixed
upon an invisible thing
and the reflection of a smile
lights up your lips,
to read upon your brow
the silent thought
that passes like a cloud
across the broad mirror of the sea,
I would give, my soul,
all that I desire:
fame, gold,
glory, genius!

When your tongue falls silent,
your breathing quickens,
your cheeks grow warm,
and you half close your dark eyes,
to see between your lashes
shine with a moist fire
the burning spark that springs
from the volcano of desires,
I would give, my soul,
all that I hope for:
faith, spirit,
earth and heaven!
